item.text: {"question_id":"4B.5","answer":"For 2023, the evidence does not establish politically neutral personnel practice and indicates material politicization and vetting risks. Tshisekedi used presidential ordinances to revoke, retire, compulsorily resign, appoint, and reassign large numbers of civilian and military judges, prosecutors, and court leaders; the stated rationale was judicial reform and rule-of-law consolidation, but the records do not give individual reasons, selection criteria, qualifications, tenure protections, or evidence of subsequent independence. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E005, BATCH-0019-E006] He also appointed Constitutional Court prosecutors, including a second presidential term for the prosecutor general, and the constitutional framework gave the president direct authority to appoint three of the Court's nine members; these facts establish presidential appointment authority, not by themselves partisan capture. [BATCH-0019-E007] Presidential appointments extended to cabinet advisers, government ministers, public-enterprise and regulatory managers, and Gécamines leadership, but the supplied records do not show whether selection was merit-based or loyalty-based. [BATCH-0015-E012, BATCH-0009-E003, BATCH-0008-E014, BATCH-0018-E004] Independent reporting described the judiciary as containing sympathetic judges and alleged ethnic stacking, while ACLED reported perceptions that CENI was politically close to the government and that Denis Kadima was close to Tshisekedi; these are significant neutrality concerns but include allegations and perceptions rather than conclusive adjudicated findings. [BATCH-0028-E021, BATCH-0010-E020] Security-sector practice raises stronger adverse concerns: surrendered Mobondo fighters were sent to military training without vetting for prior abuses, the government supported or operated alongside abusive armed groups and contracted private military personnel, and military orders during the 2023 Wazalendo protest treated protesters as enemy auxiliaries and directed security units to disperse them. [BATCH-0010-E015, BATCH-0028-E016, BATCH-0011-E019] These practices are relevant to politically neutral administration and security personnel, although armed conflict, delegated authority, and the absence of proof that Tshisekedi personally approved every operational decision limit attribution. A contrary record shows formal administrative safeguards: budget-performance rules, internal-control and audit structures, external competent audit participation, magistrate recruitment and training, police-investigation capacity, and a presidential directive that soldiers serve the nation rather than personal interests. [BATCH-0029-E004, BATCH-0029-E005, BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0009-E005, BATCH-0019-E010] Those measures demonstrate formal institutional design or stated norms, and in some cases externally supported outputs, but do not establish neutral appointments, ordinary civil-service impartiality, effective implementation, or the absence of loyalty tests or a personality
